I'll verify only the R1 delta: the two new builder guards, their signatures against the installed query builder, and the tests that claim to cover them.# Delta review P3.3–P3.4 R1 — 2026-10-04

**Verdict: GREEN.** R1 is resolved. No remaining blocker or major in this delta.

**Reviewer:** grok-4.7 / high. Read-only. No file edits, no subagents, no Pest, no database suites. The refreshed logs under `artifacts/P3-direct-writes` were not used as proof. Other product files were not re-audited.

## R1 — resolved

`WriteGuardedBuilder` now declares both missing methods. Each is `final`, declared on `AzGuard\Storage\WriteGuardedBuilder`, and its body is only `rejectDirectWrite()` (`WriteGuardedBuilder.php:40-43` and `:78-81`). That throws `UnsupportedDirectWriteException` (`:185-188`) and does not call the parent, `toBase()`, or the connection.

Installed `Illuminate\Database\Query\Builder` (Laravel 13.33.0):

| Method | Parent signature | Guard signature |
|---|---|---|
| `insertOrIgnoreReturning` | `(array $values, array $returning, array\|string\|null $uniqueBy)` | `(array $values, array $returning = ['*'], mixed $uniqueBy = null): never` |
| `updateFrom` | `(array $values)` | `(array $values): never` |

The class loaded under PHP, so the wider `mixed` third parameter and the `never` return are legal overrides. Because the methods exist on the subclass, `Eloquent\Builder::__call` no longer forwards `insertOrIgnoreReturning` through `$passthru` / `toBase()`, and no longer forwards `updateFrom` to the inner query.

A bound builder from `Storage::model()` hits these overrides for both `$builder->…()` and `$model->…()` (`Model::__call` still goes to `newQuery()`).

`DirectWritesTest` adds both methods to the builder dataset that runs for every grant model kind and for `local`, `testing`, and `production` (`DirectWritesTest.php:75`, `:79`, `:91-96`). A separate reflection test (`:98-107`) requires every public `Query\Builder` method whose name starts with `insert`, `upsert`, `update`, `increment`, `decrement`, `delete`, or `truncate` to be `final` on `WriteGuardedBuilder`. Reflection of that same set shows 16 methods, including the two from R1, all declared final on the guard. `DirectWritesEngineTest.php:26` calls both on the bound role-grant builder before the row-count and version checks.

**Observed:** the two write paths that previously compiled SQL now resolve to the guard. **Not observed:** the new Pest cases and engine runs; those logs were still being refreshed, and this pass did not execute them.
thought:
Continuing the read-only P3 review. I will verify only the R1 fix delta in the three changed files.I will read the WriteGuardedBuilder implementations to confirm they reject before forwarding, and verify test completeness.

Signature compatibility checks confirm the child overrides are valid. The `mixed` parameter type is wider than the parent's `array|string|null`, satisfying contravariance. The `never` return type is a subtype of every type, satisfying covariance.

Existing `never` return types in WriteGuardedBuilder confirm PHP 8.1+ allows this override. I will read the new methods fully to verify rejection before forwarding.

The `final` keyword ensures PHP resolves the override before any `__call` passthrough. The parent signature is `array|string|null $uniqueBy = null` returning `Collection`. The child uses `mixed $uniqueBy = null` and returns `never`.

Default values are compatible across both overrides. PHP 7.2 contravariance for parameters and covariant returns is confirmed valid. Adding `final` to the child methods is permitted because the parent methods are not final.

The `updateFrom` override is also valid. I still need to read the method bodies to confirm they call `rejectDirectWrite()` and do not invoke the parent. I also need to inspect the test completeness check to ensure it enumerates every public Query Builder write method rather than using a weak blanket assertion.

A weak completeness check that still misses a write method would be a new major blocker in the delta. The original R1 was specifically these two methods, so the delta must prove full reflection coverage over all public Query Builder writes.Verifying the reflection completeness regex covers all public write methods on Query\Builder. WriteGuardedBuilder must declare each one, not just the two new ones.

The regex covers insert, upsert, update, increment, decrement, delete, and truncate. It misses insertOrIgnoreReturning and updateFrom. WriteGuardedBuilder must declare both.

The regex also matches insertGetId, updateOrInsert, and decrementEach. I need to verify no non-write methods match it on Query\Builder. A false positive would cause WriteGuardedBuilder to declare an invalid override.

A narrow PHP reflection one-liner is acceptable here. It is not a broad test suite. I will also verify that WriteGuardedBuilder's return types are compatible with Query\Builder.

A quick PHP reflection check against the project autoload will confirm the override signatures are legal. If a signature mismatch existed, PHP would fatal during class loading.

The new insertOrIgnoreReturning method on WriteGuardedBuilder correctly shadows the parent passthru. PHP resolves it before falling back to __call.

The engine test passes a single-row associative array from grant() into insertOrIgnoreReturning. The parent accepts non-list arrays and wraps them internally.

The insertOrIgnoreReturning override throws before any SQL execution. Its signature matches the parent with one array argument and default returning and uniqueBy values.

updateFrom accepts an associative array of values.

The feature test passes a nested list of rows to updateFrom. This is valid input that also throws before SQL. The test uses toThrow, so it does not verify exception codes. This behavior mirrors the existing builder test and is not a new delta defect.

ReflectionMethod throws a ReflectionException when a method is missing from WriteGuardedBuilder, so the test fails closed. No new write methods were added to Query\Builder since the prior review.

The parent insertOrIgnoreReturning and updateFrom methods lack native return types. Adding `: never` to both child overrides is valid PHP covariant typing.

The child's third parameter is widened from `array|string|null` to `mixed`. PHP 7.2+ allows this parameter widening, but I will verify by loading the class via Composer autoload to confirm it does not fatal.

The api-manifest was regenerated as a fourth change. The user explicitly asked to read only the three code and test files, so I will not examine it.

A targeted grep will verify the api-manifest does not leak the internal WriteGuardedBuilder class or omit the new methods. A narrow git diff --stat will confirm only the three changed files were modified, avoiding any re-audit.Verifying that rejectDirectWrite still throws and does not call the parent method.

PHP loaded the class successfully, confirming the override signatures are legal. Both methods are declared final on WriteGuardedBuilder. Because they exist on the class, Eloquent Builder::__call passthrough is bypassed and the body only calls rejectDirectWrite(). The exact line number for that throw still needs to be read.

The engine test passes a single associative row to insertOrIgnoreReturning, which is valid as the first argument. Both methods throw before SQL execution. The feature test asserts UnsupportedDirectWriteException with count 1 and version 1 across kinds and environments. It calls the builder method directly rather than using pretend(). If the guard rejects before SQL, the count stays at one.

No missing methods remain in this delta. The reflection regex covers all query builder public methods starting with the relevant prefixes, and every one is final on WriteGuardedBuilder. The delete() child signature mismatch is pre-existing and outside the R1 scope.

The third parameter of insertOrIgnoreReturning is widened to mixed, which is legal and accepted by the class loader. The engine test passes a single array argument; because the override ignores all arguments and throws before SQL, this remains safe. The override bodies at lines 40-43 and 78-80 contain only rejectDirectWrite() calls with no parent or toBase forwarding.

I will check the git diff stat to confirm the three changed files contain only the expected additions and no hidden regressions. The api-manifest is not a blocker because WriteGuardedBuilder is internal.

The reflection script confirmed every matching query write is guarded. R1 is resolved and no new blocker or major issue remains in this delta.I have everything needed for the delta review.
